bounded_statement: The selected result in results/report.md (exact two-sided binomial test, 25 right-arm entries of 36 pooled trials, p = 0.0288, declared a departure from chance at the 0.05 level) is produced by entering all 36 rows — six repeated runs from each of the six whip spiders, whose independent unit is animal_id per data-description.md — as independent Bernoulli observations into scipy.stats.binomtest, a procedure that assumes row independence. With only 6 independent units and per-animal right-arm shares spanning 0.333 to 1.000, animal-level analyses of the same data (one-sample t-test on the six per-animal shares: t ≈ 1.94, df = 5, p ≈ 0.11; sign test on majority choice: 4 right vs 1 left with one tie, p = 0.375) do not reach the 0.05 level, so the stated statistical conclusion is not supported when the declared independent unit is respected.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the repeated-measures structure and per-animal tallies (6 animals, 6 trials each, shares 0.333–1.000), so the pooling is not concealed; however, disclosure does not change the fact that the selected statistical conclusion is computed by a row-independent test on repeated within-animal rows.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding in three ways. (1) Could the rows be independent despite the shared animal_id? No: the data description names animal_id as the independent-unit column, and the per-animal shares (1.000 down to 0.333) show clear between-animal heterogeneity, i.e., positive within-animal correlation, so the 36 rows are not exchangeable independent Bernoulli draws. (2) Could the conclusion survive an animal-level reanalysis, making the pooling harmless in effect? No: a one-sample t-test on the six per-animal right-arm shares against 0.5 gives mean 0.694, sd ≈ 0.245, t ≈ 1.94 with df = 5, p ≈ 0.11; a sign test on majority direction (4 animals majority-right, 1 majority-left, 1 tied) gives p = 0.375. Both exceed 0.05, so the significance claim depends on the pooled row-level test. (3) Could the report be read as claiming only a descriptive pooled share rather than an inferential conclusion? No: the [selected-result] line explicitly reports p = 0.0288 from the 36-trial binomial test and asserts 'a departure from chance at the 0.05 level.' I also verified the arithmetic from data/input.csv: 25 right-arm entries of 36 rows, matching the report, so the issue is in the inferential unit, not a computation error.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py pools every row of data/input.csv into a single exact binomial test with n = len(trials) = 36 (p_value = binomtest(n_right, n_trials, NULL_RATE, ...)), treating each of the six repeated runs per animal as an independent observation even though data-description.md designates animal_id (6 animals) as the independent unit. The repeated within-animal measurements are correlated (per-animal shares range 0.333–1.000), so the pooled test overstates the effective sample size and understates the p-value, and the report's [selected-result] claim of significance at 0.05 depends on this pseudoreplication.
